gloss: older sister (informal); big sis; young woman (familiar)

definitions.explanation: An informal, affectionate way to refer to or address one's older sister. Warmer and more casual than お{姉|ねえ}さん.
Used to address or refer to a young woman who is not one's sister, typically by children or in a friendly, informal manner.

examples.japanese: お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん、⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぼう→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{医学|いがく}→医学：01301_igaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{勉強|べんきょう}している→勉強する：00527_benkyousuru⟧。
examples.english: My big sister is studying medicine at university.

examples.japanese: ⟦{小|ちい}さい→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ついて⟦{回|まわ}っていた→回る：01150_mawaru⟧。
examples.english: When I was little, I always followed my big sister around.

examples.english: The young woman next door gave me sweets.

notes:
The informal equivalent of ⟦お{姉|ねえ}さん→お姉さん：02859_oneesan⟧, using the diminutive suffix ちゃん instead of さん. Primarily used by younger siblings, children, or in casual family settings.

FORMALITY SCALE FOR "OLDER SISTER":
- ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧: humble/plain — used when referring to one's own sister to outsiders
- お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん: informal — used within the family, especially by children
- ⟦お{姉|ねえ}さん→お姉さん：02859_oneesan⟧: polite — standard polite form, also used for young women in general
- {姉上|あねうえ}: archaic/literary — seen in period dramas and historical fiction

USAGE:
In Japanese families, younger siblings typically address their older sister as お{姉|ねえ}ちゃん rather than by name. Adults may continue using this form well into adulthood.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦お{姉|ねえ}さん→お姉さん：02859_oneesan⟧: older sister (polite); young woman — more polite and versatile
- ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧: older sister (humble/plain) — used about one's own sister in formal speech
- {姉貴|あねき}: older sister (rough/masculine) — used by males in casual or tough speech
